title: EFFORT BATCH 28: (B) a forced failure of the host's new-game start continuation hands the lobby back and the SECOND Start press starts; (A) the client's GenerateRivals, fed through the new GenerateRivals transpiler (no HGExtensions detour), mints exactly the host's 15 rival ids. The rig cannot run Proton - the field fault itself is not reproducible here
preconditions: Build with EFFORT BATCH 28 deployed (levers startfail + rivalids; charconfirm, hostnew existing). No fixture save is loaded - both machines generate a NEW world. The forced failure happens BEFORE the client joins, so the client only ever sees the second (real) start. NOTHING is saved.
oracles_absent: called inside GenerateRivals but queue empty

steps.expect_result: ^OK the next StartNewGame continuation throws once

expect_log.regex: \[Server\] StartNewGame error - lobby restored, Start can be pressed again: System.InvalidOperationException: DEV startfail lever

steps.note: FIRST press: the continuation throws once - the failure is logged once and the latch is handed back
the lever fired once and the lobby is live again (field bug: inLobby stayed False forever)

expect_log.regex: \[Server\] New game init \+ intro scene loaded
\[Wave6\] GenerateRivals starting on client; UUID queue has 15 id\(s\)

steps.note: SECOND press: a real start (not 'ignored - a start is already in flight'); the client's GenerateRivals runs from the host's 15-id feed
both machines create characters (charconfirm) and settle
the host's own minted rival ids (7 wholesale + 8 import)
THE CHECK: the client's world holds the host's ids, in order
report: the client settled into the new world
